title: ritual.json
description: A spell that requires more than one mage to cast (contracts.md §2.13). `roles` names at least two mutually exclusive tracks — the loader's `ritual-castable-by-one` check reads track.json's exclusion graph and refuses a ritual whose roles are not mutually exclusive at a threshold each role's `minNodes` actually reaches, because a ritual any one mage could eventually satisfy alone is an expensive spell wearing this shape for no reason. `effects` reuses node.json's effect shape for `primitive`, `magnitude`, `target`, `durationTicks` and `mode` — `gloss` is required here, unlike node.json, because a ritual has no cell or `v1` flag to make it conditional the way `effect-gloss-missing` does. Deliberately omits `when`, `reveals`, `control` and `transformTo`: v1 ships only `create`/`remove` rituals, and node.json's mode-payload coherence checks are tied to a cell's technique, which a ritual does not have. No ritual state is stored anywhere in the simulation — availability is derived at cast time from the living, affiliated mages of one university (`@mm/rules-magic`'s `rituals/` module); this record only declares what a valid combination of casters looks like.

roles.description: Caster roles, each pinned to a track. The schema's own floor is 1 so that a single-role record is a load failure the loader's own `ritual-too-few-roles` diagnostic explains (at least 2, per contracts.md §2.13) rather than one the schema silently forecloses before that check ever runs.

minNodes.description: Distinct nodes of `track` this caster must hold. Must be at least the threshold at which this ritual's other role(s) close this track, or a mage below that threshold could dabble in both roles' tracks at once — see the loader's ritual-castable-by-one.
